artists.biography:
Tori Amos (born Myra Ellen Amos; August 22, 1963) is an American pianist, singer-songwriter and composer. She is a classically trained musician and possesses a mezzo-soprano vocal range. Amos originally served as the lead singer of 1980s synthpop group Y Kant Tori Read, and as a solo artist was at the forefront of a number of female singer-songwriters in the early 1990s. She was also noteworthy early in her solo career as one of the few alternative rock performers to use a piano as her primary instrument. Some of her charting singles include "Crucify", "Silent All These Years", "God", "Cornflake Girl", "Caught a Lite Sneeze", "Professional Widow", "Spark", "1000 Oceans", and "A Sorta Fairytale", her most commercially successful single in the U.S. to date.
 
As of 2005, Amos had sold 12 million albums worldwide. She has been nominated for several awards, including 8 Grammy Award nominations. Amos was also named one of People Magazine's 50 Most Beautiful People in 1996.

perplexity.description:
Diving Deep Live is a live album by Tori Amos released in December 2024 on Decca Records. Recorded across her 93-date Ocean to Ocean tour throughout 2022 and 2023, the album captures performances with musical director and bassist Jon Evans and drummer Ash Soan. The standard LP version contains 12 tracks, while an expanded edition titled Diving Deeper includes 16 tracks across CD and digital platforms.

The album showcases Amos's distinctive approach to live performance, drawing from her entire discography spanning over three decades. It features career-spanning selections including well-known hits like "God" (from 1994's Under the Pink), "Cornflake Girl" (also from Under the Pink), and "Silent All These Years" (from her 1992 debut Little Earthquakes), alongside deeper cuts and B-sides such as "Ruby Through the Looking Glass," "Daisy Dead Petals," and "Sister Janet." The album demonstrates Amos's reputation for varying her setlists and arrangements, with the live renditions offering fresh interpretations of familiar material.

As Amos's third live album, Diving Deep Live serves as a testament to her virtuosity as both a musician and performer. The recordings present her work with spacious arrangements and warm, wide-ranging vocals, capturing the energy of her live shows while remaining accessible as a standalone listening experience. The album is positioned as an essential document for devoted fans while also functioning as a compelling entry point into her extensive catalog.
